body:
The new 32768-site changing-input capture test passes ordinary execution and pooled padded memcheck, but `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck --padding 32 --track-stream-ordered-races all` with the diagnostic Warp memory pool disabled reports 1536 native CUB radix-histogram atomic accesses before allocation, then aborts. The reported storage is a 17919-byte native sort scratch allocation, not a Warpower cell buffer. Earlier smaller integration tests did not expose this native scratch report. The initial 8192-site cutoff candidate had not yet undergone this lifetime check.

This may extend the previously isolated nested-graph allocation-tracking limitation (#52), but that has not yet been established for this case. Warp 1.19.0's native `sort.cu` uses asynchronous side-stream scratch allocations inside child graph capture whenever the device supports memory pools, independently of the Python allocator-enabled setting; it synchronizes that side stream and retains scratch with the graph.

- Reproduce with a standalone Warp conditional radix sort, no Warpower imports, retained arrays and explicit setup synchronization.
- Compare normal padded memcheck, full allocation-order tracking and use-after-free-only tracking, plus top-level versus conditional capture controls.
- Audit native graph and replay storage/operations; do not dismiss this as instrumentation or merge #88 until the cause is supported by controls.
- Preserve failing logs and document the actual validated configurations. No production allocator workaround or weakened certificate is authorized by this issue.

Tracked by #29 and #87; discovered during #88 validation. Hardware L40, Warp 1.19.0, Compute Sanitizer 12.9, CUDA driver 570.158.01.

A standalone Warp reproducer now exhibits the same report at both 8192 and 32768 keys, while 32768 keys pass normal padded memcheck and use-after-free-only tracking. The same 32768-key sort in a top-level capture passes full allocation-order tracking. Both sorts preserve all keys and payloads exactly under the passing configurations. A 1000-key control and the full changing-input after-free check are running.

The 1000-key conditional control passes full tracking. The complete 32768-site changing-input producer/Delaunay/consumer test passes padded use-after-free tracking with diagnostic synchronous array allocation: 1 test, 89.92 seconds, zero errors. Six pooled padded cases also passed in 334.52 seconds. Full allocation-order tracking is explicitly retained as a failure, not claimed green. The standalone controls and the original full failure are committed in 48fa35a; no production runtime change was made to work around this diagnostic.

comments.body:
PR #150 retains a fresh reproduction of this limitation during the counterbored-plate audit. Full allocation-order tracking with diagnostic synchronous arrays reports 43 CUB radix histogram accesses before allocation in 11,775-byte native scratch; ordinary padded memcheck and use-after-free/API-memory checks each pass all 11 example/audit tests with zero errors.

The standalone 8,192-key conditional Warp sort reproduces the same native kernel, instruction offset and 11,775-byte scratch report (385 errors); its top-level/full-tracking and conditional/after-free controls pass with exact keys/payloads. Production allocation is unchanged. This does not turn full allocation-order tracking green or establish arbitrary application lifetimes.

[Failure, controls, native trace and manifest](https://github.com/alecjacobson/warpower/tree/main/results/validation/vtm/mechanical), [documented scope](https://github.com/alecjacobson/warpower/blob/main/docs/mechanical-plate.md#reproduction-and-validation). The separate native trace contains three full solves, no host transfers/callbacks or replay allocation/free nodes.

title: Isolate native radix-sort scratch lifetime reports in large captured graphs
